Add support for continuous SPI reads This patch adds support for "unbounded reads" which are for continous reads to a SPI flash chip instead of reading in page size blocks. This speeds up the flash process over FTDI by quite a bit, testing the read of a 16MB part it goes from 2m11s to 0m15s. BUG=chrome-os-partner:46914 BRANCH=none TEST=test flash read with and without the patch via servo and in-system to ensure that the data is read the same in both cases. HACK: soc/tegra: pmc: Ungate DFD partition across suspend/resume There are some systems which will always hang at resume time that, for some reason, can be brought back to life be leaving the DFD partition ungated. Leave DFD ungated across suspend/resume until we figure out the root cause of these hangs. A possible side-effect from this is a very slight increase in power consumption. CHROMIUM: android: binder: Fix potential scheduling-while-atomic Commit f1e7f0a724f6 ("android: binder: Disable preemption while holding the global binder lock.") re-enabled preemption around most of the sites where calls to potentially sleeping functions were made, but missed __alloc_fd(), which can sleep if the fdtable needs to be resized. FROMLIST: usb: dwc2: host: Fix remote wakeup when not in DWC2_L2 In commit 734643dfbdde ("usb: dwc2: host: add flag to reflect bus state") we changed dwc2_port_suspend() not to set the lx_state anymore (instead it sets the new bus_suspended variable). This introduced a bug where we would fail to detect device insertions if: 1. Plug empty hub into dwc2 2. Plug USB flash drive into the empty hub. 3. Wait a few seconds 4. Unplug USB flash drive 5. Less than 2 seconds after step 4, plug the USB flash drive in again. The dwc2_hcd_rem_wakeup() function should have been changed to look at the new bus_suspended variable. Let's fix it. Since commit b46146d59fda ("usb: dwc2: host: resume root hub on remote wakeup") talks about needing the root hub resumed if the bus was suspended, we'll include it in our test. It appears that the "port_l1_change" should only be set to 1 if we were in DWC2_L1 (the driver currently never sets this), so we'll update the former "else" case based on this test. BUG=chrome-os-partner:46812 TEST=see bug Change-Id: I0aae4d01753f041d19c64f76ebae88b9d94db9de Fixes: 734643dfbdde ("usb: dwc2: host: add flag to reflect bus state") Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/7467511/) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/308181 Reviewed-by: Julius Werner <jwerner@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: drm/nouveau: add per channel fifo mutex The mutex inside nouveau_cli is vastly abused in concurrent access control. Any operation from the same process will be blocked on the same mutex. This lazy protection impose a rather low cap on multi- channel performance. We have seen cases where pushbuf worker thread got delayed on that mutex for more than 100ms just waiting to submit pushbuf to GPU, not counting delay on the same mutex when pushbuf was queued through nouveau_gem_ioctl_pushbuf_2(). While ideal solution is to factorize the mutex into multiple components, leaving only nouveau_abi16 and nouveau_cli under its protection, such refactoring would be huge and of high risk. Thus we only release the most performance critical part, pushbuf submit, from the control of this mutex. Further refactoring should be considered depending on performance outcome. Functions with fifo access (Need to hold chan->fifo_lock when calling): - nouveau_fence_new() - nouveau_fence_emit() - nouveau_fence_emit_initted() - nouveau_dma_wait() - nv50_dma_*() - nv*_bo_move_*() - BEGIN_*() - OUT_RING() - FIRE_RING() - WIND_RING() Utility functions already acquire fifo_lock on their own as needed: - nouveau_fence_sync() - nouveau_bo_sync() BUG=chrome-os-partner:46741 TEST=Run monkey test for camera on smuag, no fence timeout. Change-Id: I800e15c0b10cb371a32dd427d7af2a46ea6292a5 Signed-off-by: Xia Yang <xiay@nvidia.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/307949 Reviewed-by: David Ung <davidu@nvidia.com> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Haixia Shi <hshi@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: clk: tegra: dfll: fix logic for building lookup table The lookup table entries are fixed, and the voltages in these entries are distributed based on minimum and maximum voltages and each voltages in opp table. Since the last entry is reserved for maximum voltage, we found the voltage in the next to last entry is not accurate enough for the next to last frequency in some SKUs. This causes the DFLL driver cannot find a proper voltage index when CPUFreq driver set expected frequency as the next to last frequency. This patch fixes the original logic to force to use find_vdd_map_entry_exact() for the next to last frequency, this will make the selected voltage are more accurate.
